notes:
Passed on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware run and no human review. This repository is a multi-instrument SCPI library: the package binds the PowerSupply entry symbol only, configured for the Siglent SPD3303X/SPD3303X-E, and does not cover Oscilloscope, FunctionGenerator, ReportTemplate or WaveformData. Covered: output 1 voltage and current setpoints, tracking mode, measured output 1 voltage and current, *IDN?, SYST:ERR?, and an e-stop that writes OUTPut CH1,OFF and OUTPut CH2,OFF. Not covered: channels 2 and 3 setpoints, output-state readback (the SPD3303X status word is bit-encoded and this text command map cannot decode it), the waveform/timer/remote-sense subsystems, and the oscilloscope/function-generator classes. The tracking readback sends OUTP:TRACK?, which the upstream code defines; the clone's own inventory marks that query form as undocumented in the quick-start guide (docs/development/wire-form-inventory.md:299), so readback may not work on hardware. G4.REF_VALUE x2 is reported for voltage and current: the cited line scpi_control/psu_models.py:77 shows the 30 V and 3 A upper bounds but not the lower bound 0, which the same Limit object cannot cite from the other file (scpi_control/power_supply_output.py:76 and :116); the reason text names both lines and the min value is not omitted. The fake is a hand-written command model, not the upstream mock under scpi_control/connection/mock, because package code must not import the read-only clone and a deterministic state model is easier to reason about; every canned number is marked '# placeholder' in fake.py and none is used as a Fact, Limit or reference. Site-limits.example.json narrows voltage to 12 V, current to 1 A and tracking to 0/1 for the example bench. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
